acceptance_criteria.condition: The Causal Repair Card appears before the detailed causal policy and requires symptom/invariant separation, owner path, alternative hypothesis, discriminating probe, and calibrated conclusion.

The v6 runner supports multi-file workspaces, explicit relative edit scope, hidden-test injection only after Agent exit, and an atomic checkpoint after each complete pair; an incomplete pair is marked ineligible without retry.
The fresh corpus contains exactly 20 unique tasks across all preregistered strata; every buggy workspace fails its public suite and every reference workspace passes public plus hidden tests.
The v6 effect envelope hashes the Skill, prompts, generator, runner, scorer, corpus manifest, task plan, and statistical thresholds before collection and contains no trials.

invariants: v4 and v5 hidden contracts are not reused as v6 task inputs.
The repair Agent receives a public task workspace and a snapshot containing only SKILL.md; hidden tests and reference repairs remain scorer-only.
A non-complete Agent condition invalidates the collection; the runner records the interruption and does not silently retry or analyze partial pairs.
An `improved` result, if later observed, can support only the preregistered fixed model, Harness, corpus, Skill revision, and hidden scorer scope.

safeguards.name: front-loaded causal owner card
safeguards.rationale: The short owner-first sequence is placed before detailed gates so it is available before a repair edit.

safeguards.name: scorer-only hidden workspace
safeguards.rationale: The scorer copies the candidate into a temporary directory and injects hidden tests only after the Agent process exits; raw Agent artifacts never contain hidden files.

safeguards.name: pair checkpoint and interruption gate
safeguards.rationale: The output is atomically replaced after each pair and an incomplete condition produces an ineligible interrupted record rather than a partial statistic.

design_boundary.rationale: SKILL.md owns the causal workflow; the v6 runner owns execution/checkpoint state; the v6 scorer owns hidden-contract execution; the generator owns fixture materialization.

dependency_audit.rationale: The new protocol uses only Python standard library, Git, unittest, and existing Codex CLI surfaces.

extension_decision.rationale: No public application extension point is introduced.

data_ownership.rationale: Public task trees, hidden scorer trees, and raw trial artifacts have separate owners and lifecycle boundaries; hidden data never enters Agent workspaces.

error_model.rationale: Public failure, hidden failure, scope violation, timeout, nonzero Agent exit, and interrupted collection remain distinct recorded outcomes.

contract_evolution.rationale: The existing analyzer remains unchanged; v6 adds a separate manifest and runner contract while v4/v5 protocols remain replayable.

operational_budget.rationale: The runner declares Agent and scorer timeouts, kills timed-out process groups, and records elapsed time and test timeout state.

threat_boundary.rationale: Hidden tests and reference repairs are outside the Agent input boundary; native Codex isolation is explicitly treated as protocol isolation, not a container security boundary.

delivery_lifecycle.rationale: The Skill card, v6 scripts, corpus, prompts, preregistration, tests, README, reference protocol, and evidence are frozen as one atomic verified change before any trial.

release_recovery.rationale: This is an offline evaluation package and performs no production rollout.

data_migration.rationale: No production or persistent application schema is changed.

configuration_secrets.rationale: The experiment declares non-secret model/Harness IDs and sanitizes user-site/bytecode environment behavior; no credential is stored.

dependency_supply_chain.rationale: No dependency or lockfile is added.

operational_knowledge.rationale: README and effect-evaluation reference describe the v6 boundary, hidden injection order, checkpoint rule, and interpretation limit.

reproducibility.rationale: The manifest, source tree hashes, prompt hashes, generator/runner/scorer hashes, fixed seed, task strata, model, Harness, and statistical stopping rule are preregistered.

independent_review.reviewer: deterministic corpus and runner contract tests
independent_review.notes: The tests independently exercise hidden injection, path scope, checkpoint completion/interruption, manifest hashes, public fixture failure, and reference repair success. They do not pre-judge the future paired treatment outcome.

supporting_artifacts.summary: Normative Skill with the front-loaded Causal Repair Card.
Skill contract tests including card placement and owner-first requirements.
Hash-linked corpus test proving each buggy public suite fails and each reference suite passes while preserving and separating the historical v6 runner digest.
Post-interruption corrected runner with explicit multi-file scope, empty-destination isolation, and the frozen v6 protocol digest retained in preregistration/result.
Runner tests for hidden-copy isolation, randomized order, completed checkpoints, interruption ineligibility, pre-created-directory seeding, and stale-destination rejection.
Regression test tying the v6 interruption report to the retained raw tree and result bundle.
Generic scorer that injects hidden tests only into a temporary post-exit copy.
Frozen 20-task manifest with public/hidden tree digests and explicit edit scopes.
Pre-run v6 effect envelope with no trials and complete protocol hashes.

remaining_risks: No v6 Agent condition has run yet; this artifact cannot support a Skill-effect claim.
Native Codex workspace isolation is protocol isolation rather than a filesystem/container security boundary.
Upstream model-service interruption can still make a complete paired run ineligible; the checkpoint preserves the evidence but cannot create a valid statistic.
